name: Company wizard on a fresh installation (guided first-run setup)
description:
WRITTEN FROM: codx-junior-website (hosted provisioning). Our signup collects the basics in a form (admin user/password, AI provider + key, model, endpoint) and passes them to your installer as CODX_JUNIOR_ADMIN_* / CODX_JUNIOR_AI_* in settings.env. That covers the machine-readable part. What it cannot do is guide a person: a fresh install lands on a workspace with no company, no projects and no obvious first step, so a user who did not come through our signup (self-hosted, docker run, a customer who opens their box directly) is on their own.

THE ASK (a "company wizard" on a fresh installation)
On the first authenticated session of an installation that has no company yet, show a short guided setup instead of an empty workspace:
1. Company/organisation: name, description, primary language, optional logo/colour. Creates the company record the rest of the product already expects.
2. Owner/admin account: when CODX_JUNIOR_ADMIN_* was NOT provided, ask for the admin user + password here (hash and store, never echo). When it WAS provided, skip this step and show who the admin is (read only).
3. AI provider: pick provider (ollama / openai / anthropic / deepseek / custom), enter key, model and endpoint. Store it with the same keys we already write (CODX_JUNIOR_AI_PROVIDER / _API_KEY / _MODEL / _ENDPOINT) so both paths converge on one config surface.
4. Optional but valuable: a "try it" check — call the configured provider once and report reachable/unreachable (this is also what ticket ae60331d asks /api/health to expose).
5. Finish: land in the product with the company selected.

Requirements
- Idempotent and skippable: it runs only while no company exists; it must never re-run over a configured installation, and there is an explicit "skip for now" that does not lose the admin bootstrap.
- Non-interactive safe: with CODX_JUNIOR_NON_INTERACTIVE=true (DEPLOYMENT-CONTRACT.md) the wizard is never a terminal prompt, only UI on first login. Nothing may block the container start waiting for input.
- Same config surface as DEPLOYMENT-CONTRACT.md: values the wizard writes must be readable back by our provisioning (so our portal can show what a workspace is configured with) and must not be duplicated in a second place.
- Never log or echo the API key or the admin password; store the key with the same protection you already use for settings.

WHY IT MATTERS FOR US
Our hosted flow currently provisions a workspace that can look "ready" while being unable to answer a single message (provider ollama, no key). A guided first-run setup closes that class of empty install for every deployment path, and reduces what our own signup form has to collect.

If this is already in your backlog, decline or link this card and we will follow yours — this is the tracked reference on our side.
